Today, we're featuring another episode of The Rewind, in which Howard looks back on some of his memos over the years,
discusses their origins, and considers their relevance to today's financial environment.
In this episode, Howard reflects on the memo On the Couch, which was originally published on January 14th, 2016.
Next week, we'll hear Howard's thoughts on what does the market know, a related memo which was published five days later.
here's Howard 2015 was a difficult period it was a down year in most markets it was the first down year since the global financial crisis so of course everybody was nervous everybody was concerned about a replay of the global financial crisis or something like it or at minimum a recession so when 2016 began the market got off to its worst start I think in history with a substantial

when everybody believes that things will only get better forever.

thesis: Howard Marks argues that market psychology fluctuates inordinately between extremes of optimism and pessimism, often ignoring gradual negatives until they become overwhelming, at which point reactions are swift and irrational. He illustrates this by explaining that falling oil prices are frequently misinterpreted as purely negative for the market, whereas the price drop itself triggers supply reductions and demand increases that naturally lead to a reversion to the mean.
